Support resources

Need Help?

That’s okay. So did I at one point. These resources are meant to help people in crisis find a safer next step.

If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 911 now. Always confirm details directly with official providers.
Important disclaimer

The content presented on this site is intended solely for informational, educational, and awareness-building purposes. Nothing on this site should be interpreted as legal, medical, psychological, social work, housing, financial, or emergency advice. No professional-client relationship is created through viewing this content. While efforts have been made to provide accurate and relevant information based in research and cited literature, no guarantees are made regarding completeness, accuracy, timeliness, or applicability to any specific individual, school, region, or organization. Viewers are responsible for confirming information with qualified professionals, official services, or appropriate community organizations.

These resources are meant to help people in crisis, but always consult with a professional or official service.

Need a place to sleep tonight?

Le Bunker - Dans la rue

Emergency shelter, safe place to sleep, food, shower, laundry, and support.

Age 12-21

Call: 514-524-0029

What to do: Call first and ask if there is space tonight.

Open resource
Scan or open

Are you 12-17 and need help now?

En Marge 12-17

Emergency shelter, short-term help, support workers, information, and referrals.

Age 12-17

Call: 514-849-7117

hebergement@enmarge1217.ca

What to do: Call and say: I need a safe place tonight. Can you help me?

Open resource
Scan or open

Need help finding food, shelter, clothes, or services near you?

211 Québec

Local resource navigation for food, shelter, clothing, legal help, mental health, youth services, and more.

Call: 211

What to do: Tell them your city or postal code and what you need tonight.

Open resource
Scan or open

Need someone to talk to right now?

Info-Social 811

A psychosocial worker when you are stressed, scared, overwhelmed, in crisis, or unsure what to do next.

Call: 811, option 2

What to do: Say: I need help and I do not know where to go.

Open resource
Scan or open

Are you 12-25 and need health, mental health, or social support?

Aire ouverte

Free help for young people with stress, mental health, relationships, housing problems, health questions, or family issues.

Age 12-25

What to do: Find the Aire ouverte closest to you.

Open resource
Scan or open

Need to text or call someone confidentially?

Jeunesse, j’écoute / Kids Help Phone

Free, confidential support for kids, teens, and young adults across Canada.

Call: 1-800-668-6868

Text 686868

What to do: You do not need to explain everything perfectly. Start with: I need help.

Open resource
Scan or open

Need teen support in Québec?

Tel-jeunes

Support for stress, family, school, relationships, violence, emotions, or anything that feels too heavy.

Call: 1-800-263-2266

What to do: Contact them when you need to talk to someone who will not judge you.

Open resource
Scan or open

Worried about your safety or someone else’s safety?

Suicide.ca / 1-866-APPELLE

24/7 support if you feel unsafe, in crisis, or worried about someone.

Call: 1-866-277-3553

Text 535353

What to do: Call, text, or chat. If there is immediate danger, call 911.

Open resource
Scan or open

Need help from someone in your neighbourhood?

ROCQTR - Travail de rue

Find street work organizations in Québec.

Call: 514-575-0300

What to do: Ask how to reach a street worker near your neighbourhood.

Open resource
Scan or open

Looking for a youth organization near you?

Regroupement des maisons des jeunes du Québec

Find youth centres and youth support organizations.

Call: 514-725-2686

What to do: Use the directory or call to locate a youth centre close to you.

Services to analyze your substances

CACTUS Montréal - Checkpoint

Substance analysis and risk-reduction conversation.

What to do: Check hours and current service details before going.

Open resource
Scan or open

Where to find naloxone for those aged 14 and older

Naloxone in Québec

No-charge naloxone access through pharmacies and some community organizations.

Age 14+

What to do: Use the map and call ahead if possible. In an overdose, call 911 immediately.
